title.narrative: Malakal and Panyikang Emergency Response project Upper Nile State – South Sudan

description.narrative: 130,000 people have been displaced in Upper Nile due to the expansion of the conflict between South Sudan People's Defense Forces (SSPDF) and armed youth to counties such as Malakal and Fashoda. According to an inter-agency assessment conducted on 26th May 2025 by humanitarian partners in Malakal, both Malakal and Fashoda county are hosting a total of about 7,734 (Malakal = 4,434 & Fashoda = 3,300) IDPs. This displacement of population in Upper Nile State came amidst significant numbers of returnees already stressing services and with South Sudan battling outbreak of cholera further exacerbating the humanitarian situation of the displaced population. Trócaire, through its partner Caritas Diocese of Malakal (CDOM) is already implementing programmes in Upper Nile State in the counties of Panyikang, and Fashoda. However, the project does not have the capacity to respond to the spike in displaced persons and exacerbation of cholera risk due to the poor sanitation prevalent in the IDP settlements. Therefore, this project will be implemented by Trocaire’s local partner ACRA to supplement the already existing projects.
